contract: Road user a is moving backward: it moves against the direction its body points. It is observed as the component of a's velocity (kin.velocity) along a's heading (kin.heading), the dot product of the velocity with the heading as a formula reads it normalised, being below minus speed_tol: the part of a's motion that runs against its heading exceeds the speed the source cannot tell from rest. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of the gear selected, of the path a has followed or will follow, of where a is, or of why it moves so. Not denoted: a road user at rest, or one whose velocity component against its heading is at or below speed_tol; a road user moving forward. Where a's velocity or heading is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed against the heading at or below which motion is not told from rest: the source's speed resolution

elements.span: the component of a's velocity (kin.velocity) along a's heading (kin.heading)
elements.justification: kin.velocity is the 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame) and kin.heading the 'direction the body points' (unit vector, world frame, read normalised); their dot product is the signed speed along the heading, negative when the body moves against the way it points. kin.gear is not read: its contract says it is 'Not a stand-in for: the direction of motion — ... backing is read from kinematics'.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car with heading (1, 0) moves with velocity (-1.5, 0) m/s: the component along its heading is -1.5 m/s, below minus speed_tol; the concept holds.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same car moves with velocity (2.0, 0.1) m/s: the component along its heading is positive; it is moving forward and the concept does not hold.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car's heading is known but the source supplies no velocity at the observation; whether it moves backward is unknown.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bus,
other than a tour bus,
shall: Not stand or park a bus
at a bus stop or an origin or destination point
for a period of time longer than has been designated for such bus stop or origin or destination point
in accordance with Section 11.60.010 [DEF-LVMC-11-60-010].

elements.justification: 'bus' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus; ru.aggregate is claimed with that id and never expanded into classes. 'The operator of' names who controls the bus, read through the bus's own conduct (agency narrowing). Same mapping as the index's 'The operator of a bus,'.

'tour bus' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus ('a motor vehicle, other than a limousine, which is designed, maintained and used to transport more than six persons ... to or from hotels, motels, casinos'); a subject that carries it is excused. Same mapping as the index's 'other than a tour bus,'.

'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250: 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155: 'the standing of a vehicle') both begin with a halt; drv.motion.complete_halt denotes the road user at rest ('its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance'). The length of the halt is what s5 compares; the passenger-loading exclusions of the two definitions are what the designated period allows at a stop. 'a bus' is the admitted aggregate again.

st.curb_zone of kind bus_stop ('a signed or marked length of curb; kind ∈ {..., bus_stop, ...}') and st.transit_stop ('a bus stop, bench, shelter or platform for public transport passengers') are the stop and the origin or destination point the City Traffic Engineer designates by signs; rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (..., curb zone, ...)') anchors the bus to the one it stands at. Same atoms as the index's 'at any place other than a bus stop, bus stand or the origin or destination point'.

Nearest atoms only (gap): the words borrow from LVMC 11.60.010 [DEF-LVMC-11-60-010] that “he may designate the length of time that a bus may stand or park at each”, so the period is the one designated for 'such bus stop' — the stop s4 singles out — and is designated by its signs. kin.time with the time since the halt began measures how long the bus has stood; dev.zone_sign and dev.regulatory_sign carry a 'conditions' attribute that lists 'a duration limit', but no measure of §11 reads it and prim.conditions_hold decides only time windows, occupancy and class conditions. No term yields the designated period, so the comparison cannot be written.

compositions.quote: he may designate the length of time that a bus may stand or park at each

applicability: The subject is a bus (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus) and not a tour bus (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-150::tour_bus), at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its footprint overlapping a bus-stop curb zone or a transit stop s (rel.occupies).
obligation: The time elapsed since the subject's halt at s began (the time since drv.motion.complete_halt last became true, while it occupies s) does not exceed the period designated for s by its posted sign. That period has no measure a formula reads (gap on s5): the node is not coded until the gap is decided.

narrowings.why: 'The operator of a bus' is read through the bus's controlled motion and halts, whoever or whatever controls it.
The stop or origin or destination point 'designated' by the Traffic Engineer is read by the presence of the signed or marked curb zone or transit stop.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A transit bus halts in a bus_stop curb zone whose sign posts a 5-minute limit and stays at rest for 20 minutes.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same bus halts 2 minutes in the bus_stop curb zone and leaves.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A tour bus halts 20 minutes in the same curb zone: the subject carries the excepted tour-bus class.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A transit bus stands 20 minutes in the bus_stop curb zone; the zone sign's legend is not read by the source, so the designated period is unknown.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

gaps.proposal: `dev.posted_duration_limit` | the longest duration of standing or parking that a posted sign states for the stop, stand or region it designates or governs, read from the sign's legend as a duration (s) a formula compares with an elapsed time; absent where the legend is not read **Not a stand-in for:** whether the sign's time windows hold now (`prim.conditions_hold`), or a time of day (`env.civil_time`) | general — it decides when a halt at a designated stop becomes a breach: how long the road user may stand there
gaps.nearest: dev.zone_sign / dev.regulatory_sign: their 'conditions' attribute lists 'a duration limit' but §11 gives it no measure and prim.conditions_hold reads only time windows, occupancy and class; kin.time with the time since the halt began measures the halt but not the designated period; a reading parameter would fix one period for every stop, whereas the words make it the period designated for 'such bus stop'.

segmentation.text: The operator of a taxicab
shall not stand or park such vehicle
upon any street
at any place other than in a taxicab stand so designated as provided herein.
This provision shall not prevent the operator of a taxicab from temporarily stopping
in accordance with other stopping or parking regulations
at any place for the purpose of and while actually engaged in the expeditious loading or unloading of passengers.

elements.justification: 'taxicab' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab ('a motor vehicle which is properly licensed under State and local law to provide taxicab service'); claimed as the aggregate, never as ru.taxicab. 'The operator of' is read through the taxicab's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250: 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers') contains 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155: 'the standing of a vehicle ... otherwise than temporarily'), so 'stand or park' is standing. drv.motion.parked denotes the road user at rest at every observation of a window of length min_duration ('A halt shorter than min_duration ... is not denoted'); with min_duration = p.standing_min_duration the purpose exclusion of the definition is read through the halt's duration (purpose narrowing). 'such vehicle' is the taxicab, and 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, which the taxicab carries. Same concept as the index's 'shall: Not stand or park such vehicle'.

'street' (DEF-NRS-484A-265: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city') is a highway: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' and is not a stand-in for the roadway, which the words do not narrow to. The city-limit qualification is the territorial scope of this city ordinance, within which every highway is a street. rel.occupies anchors the taxicab to the way. Same atoms as the index's 'upon any street'.

'taxicab stand' (DEF-NRS-484B-067: 'a fixed area in a highway parallel and adjacent to the curb or edge of the highway and set aside for taxicabs to stand for passengers') is st.curb_zone of kind taxicab_stand ('a signed or marked length of curb; kind ∈ {..., taxicab_stand, ...}'); rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (..., curb zone, ...)') places the standing taxicab in it. 'so designated as provided herein' is read by the presence of the signed or marked stand (status narrowing).

'temporarily stopping' (stopping, DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle') is a halt of the taxicab: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation'. A halt that ends before p.standing_min_duration is not drv.motion.parked, so the temporary stop the words protect is outside the obligation of s2.

'for the purpose of and while actually engaged in the expeditious loading or unloading of passengers' is a purpose, read through the halt's duration: a halt no longer than p.standing_min_duration, the passenger pick-up dwell at the curb, is not drv.motion.parked with that min_duration ('A halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out, is not denoted'), so it is excused 'at any place'.

residues.why: 'This provision shall not prevent' a temporary passenger stop: the words leave such a stop to the other stopping and parking regulations, which judge it by their own rules. A temporary stop that breaches another regulation is that regulation's violation; under this provision it is neither standing nor parking (DEF-NRS-484A-250, DEF-NRS-484A-155), so this rule's verdict is the same whether or not the stop complies with the others.

applicability: The subject is a taxicab (ru.aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-140::taxicab, a vehicle) whose footprint overlaps a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway) at the observation.
obligation: Wherever the subject stands — drv.motion.parked(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration = p.standing_min_duration, i.e. at rest at every observation of the last p.standing_min_duration — its footprint overlaps a curb zone of kind taxicab_stand (rel.occupies, st.curb_zone). A halt shorter than p.standing_min_duration, the temporary stop for loading or unloading passengers, is not standing and is compliant at any place.

narrowings.why: 'The operator of a taxicab' is read through the taxicab's controlled motion and halts, whoever or whatever controls it.

The definitions' exclusion of a halt 'for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers' is read through the halt's duration: standing is a halt longer than p.standing_min_duration.
'so designated as provided herein' is read by the presence of the signed or marked taxicab_stand curb zone.
The purpose of loading or unloading passengers is read through a halt no longer than p.standing_min_duration.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab halts at the curb of a city highway, outside any taxicab_stand curb zone, and stays at rest for 5 minutes.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab halts within a taxicab_stand curb zone of the highway and stays at rest for 5 minutes.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab stands for 5 minutes in a private parking lot whose footprint lies on no highway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab is at the curb of a highway outside any taxicab stand for 5 minutes; the source supplies no speed, so whether it stands is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab halts 30 seconds at the curb outside any taxicab stand, a passenger boards, and it drives off: the halt is a temporary stop, not standing.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.standing_min_duration
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as receiving or discharging passengers or loading rather than standing: a passenger pick-up dwell at the curb
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_52_040_A; curbside passenger dwell times of taxi and ride-hail pick-up studies

segmentation.text: Any cab,
upon leaving any stand designated in accordance with the provisions of this Section,
shall execute a right-hand turn,
when a sign is posted giving notice of this requirement,
at the first street intersection after it leaves such stand.

elements.justification: No definition applies to 'cab' in this law (the definitions table lists none), so it is mapped like other words: ru.taxicab, 'passenger vehicle for hire, identifiable by its markings', is the class a cab is. No aggregate is admitted for the word here, so the class atom is the carrier.

The 'stand designated in accordance with the provisions of this Section' (a taxistand section) is the taxicab stand, st.curb_zone of kind taxicab_stand ('a signed or marked length of curb; kind ∈ {..., taxicab_stand, ...}'). The table resolves 'stand' to DEF-NRS-484A-250, which defines the act of halting; the noun here names the place, so the definition's words are not the carrier. 'leaving' is the event at which the cab's footprint ceases to overlap that curb zone (rel.occupies false, having been true at the previous observation). Designation is read by the stand's presence (status).

drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(a, r) denotes that 'Road user a has made a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r', with its heading change since entry in the right-turn band; it takes the intersection as its region argument, so the turn is judged at the intersection s5 singles out. kin.yaw_rate and rel.occupies are the atoms it reads.

The posted sign is a dev.regulatory_sign of code right_turn_only ('a point regulation by catalogue code, ... right_turn_only'), read where it governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region the cab occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation it leaves the stand, with its conditions holding for the cab (prim.conditions_hold: 'any occupancy or class condition is met'), so a notice limited to taxicabs is read as such. The sign is a condition, not the turn itself ('a prohibition sign is a condition').

'the first street intersection after it leaves such stand' is the intersection r (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet') whose exit the turn concept recognizes, such that since the observation the cab left 'such stand' — the same curb zone s2 binds — its footprint has overlapped no intersection other than r (rel.occupies). A city intersection is a street intersection within this ordinance's territorial scope.

applicability: The subject is a taxicab (ru.taxicab). At the observation t its footprint ceases to overlap an intersection r (rel.occupies, st.intersection: false at t, true at t-1). Earlier, at an observation d, it left a taxicab_stand curb zone k (overlap of k true at d-1, false at d) while a regulatory sign of code right_turn_only whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold) governed (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupied at d; and at every observation from d to t its footprint overlapped no intersection other than r (written with since: [for every intersection q not the same as r, not rel.occupies(subject, q)] since [the departure from k with the sign condition]).
obligation: At t, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(subject, r) holds, with step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min and u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min: the cab's passage through the first intersection after leaving the stand was a turn to the right.

narrowings.why: 'designated in accordance with the provisions of this Section' is read by the presence of the signed or marked taxicab_stand curb zone.

A sign 'giving notice of this requirement' is read as a posted right_turn_only regulatory sign that governs the travel region the cab occupies as it leaves the stand and whose conditions hold for the cab; its posting is read by its presence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab leaves a taxicab_stand curb zone into a lane governed by a right_turn_only sign, reaches the first intersection and goes straight through it: at its exit the heading change since entry is about 0 degrees.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same taxicab turns right through the first intersection: at its exit the heading change since entry is about -90 degrees.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab leaves the stand into a lane no right_turn_only sign governs and goes straight through the first intersection.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source supplies no yaw rate while the cab is in the intersection, so the heading change through it is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The taxicab turns right through the first intersection after the signed stand, then goes straight through a second intersection: at the exit of the second, an intersection other than it was occupied since the departure, so it is not the first.

onset.words: the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r
onset.justification: The turn concept's act begins at the cab's entry into the intersection r, marked by rel.occupies rising on r.

occasion.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.

under_way.justification: Inside the act the cab is within r since its entry and its heading is changing (kin.yaw_rate), which no observation before the entry shows; no span of this node is read while the act is under way.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; turning-movement classification in trajectory analysis

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; turning-movement classification in trajectory analysis

segmentation.text: Every driver of a vehicle
approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign

shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway
before entering the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; claimed as the aggregate. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) names who controls the vehicle, a relational role, not membership: read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

The approach is the carrier c the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection r (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'); the stop intersection is 'indicated by a stop sign' where a dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') governs c (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ...'). st.travel_region is the kind of c, st.intersection the kind of r. Same atoms as the index's 'approaching the intersection' plus the stop sign.

'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies: 'complete cessation from movement', drv.motion.complete_halt. The three places are read through the approach carrier c, in the order the words list. (1) The crosswalk 'on the near side of the intersection' is the st.crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of: 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); 'before entering' it is a halt with the footprint off it (rel.occupies), short of it along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along along st.lane_direction, positive) and within the stop-point tolerance (st.region_geometry ground distance). Distance never stands for belonging: the association is st.entrance_of. (2) 'if there is no crosswalk' holds where the crosswalks' entrance lists are observed and none marks c ('where the source observes a line's entrances its list is complete'); the st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', recorded as marking c, is then the place: a halt not past it along c's direction, body within the tolerance; 'clearly marked' is read by the represented line (status). (3) 'if none': no stop line marks c either (lists observed); the point nearest the intersecting highway before entering the intersection is c's entrance end at r (st.intersection): a halt off r, short of r along c's direction, body within the tolerance of r — the ontology's approach convention reads the edge of the intersection as the carrier's entrance end, which is the point nearest the intersecting highway and the one with the widest view along it.

The event the halt precedes: the vehicle's footprint comes to overlap the intersection r (rel.occupies true at the observation, false at the previous one), r being the region st.lane_enters names for c.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that enters an intersection r at the judged observation t — its footprint overlaps r at t and not at t-1 (rel.occupies) — having occupied at t-1 a carrier c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is r (st.lane_enters(c, r)), and a stop sign (dev.stop_sign) governs c (dev.governs).
obligation: Duty of an act before an event (approach convention). Event: the entry into r at t through c; the duty is judged at t. Act: a halt of the subject (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance) at the governing place, read through c. Place, in the order the words list: (1) where a crosswalk x is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of(x, c)): a halt at which the footprint does not overlap x (rel.occupies), the subject is short of x along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along of x along st.lane_direction of c, positive) and the body-to-x ground distance (st.region_geometry) is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (2) else, where the crosswalk lists are observed and none marks c, and a stop line l is recorded as marking c: a halt at which the subject is not past l along c's direction (offset not negative) and the body-to-l distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (3) else, where the crosswalk and stop-line lists are observed and none marks c: a halt at which the footprint does not overlap r, the subject is short of r along c's direction, and the body-to-r distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance. Where several marks of the governing kind mark c, a halt in the zone of any of them it has not passed counts. History bound: the search runs back from t-1 and ends at the approach start — the last observation before t at which the subject, on a carrier the governing mark is recorded as marking, is outside that mark's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it, farther than p.stop_point_tolerance; with several marks, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into r, whichever is later. Nothing else ends it: not the start of the recording, a first observation, another intersection or mark, or a distance travelled. Crossing the mark, moving on toward r, a change of carrier or lateral move within the same entry, a reverse that stays within the zone and speed noise begin no new approach; only an observed exit from the zone upstream does, and the act is then owed again. Verdict: the act found → compliant; the search reaches the approach start or the previous entry without it → violated; it reaches neither (the recording begins first, or a speed or place in between is unobserved) without the act → unknown. Missing evidence: the entry is unknown, never absent, where t-1 does not show the subject on a mapped carrier with an observed association to r (no earlier observation, no mapped carrier, association unobserved); an unobserved dev.governs of c, or an unobserved association of a mark with c, makes the verdict unknown only where it turns on it — a halt found at a place known to govern, and an association the source excludes, are decided whatever the missing fact.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

The stop intersection 'indicated by a stop sign' is read by a stop sign the source records as governing the approach carrier c; a sign recorded only as governing the intersection itself is not read as facing c.
'clearly marked' is read by the represented stop line; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

The point nearest the intersecting highway 'where the driver has a view of approaching traffic' is read as c's entrance end, the edge of r, within p.stop_point_tolerance: no point nearer the intersecting highway lies before the intersection, and the view along it is widest there; the view itself (st.sight_along_way) is not compared with a bound.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on lane c, governed by a stop sign, with a crosswalk recorded as marking c, approaches from 40 m at 10 m/s, rolls over the crosswalk at 4 m/s and enters the intersection without ever being at rest.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car comes to rest 1 m short of the crosswalk, off it, then proceeds and enters the intersection.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the intersection through a lane governed by a traffic signal and by no stop sign.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions the stop sign governs.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No crosswalk marks c (lists observed); a stop line marks c; the car comes to rest 1 m short of the line and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Neither a crosswalk nor a stop line marks c (lists observed); the car comes to rest 1 m short of the intersection's edge, off it, and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A crosswalk marks c; the car comes to rest 20 m short of it, moves on and enters the intersection without halting again: the halt lies before the approach start.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already 1 m short of the crosswalk marking c, moving at 3 m/s; it enters the intersection without a recorded halt, and no recorded observation shows it outside the stopping zone upstream.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the observation at which the car was outside the crosswalk's stopping zone upstream lies before the recording, so whether it halted within the zone before the recording began is not observed

param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching a yield sign
if required for safety to stop

shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing). Same mapping as the index's 'The driver of a vehicle'.

dev.yield_sign is the 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt'; the vehicle approaches it where it occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c the sign governs (dev.governs) and whose entrance end is the intersection r (st.lane_enters). The intersection is named by 'the nearest side of the intersection'; st.travel_region is the kind of c.

'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies: 'complete cessation from movement', drv.motion.complete_halt. The places are read through the approach carrier c, in the order listed. (1) The crosswalk 'on the nearest side of the intersection' is the st.crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of: 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); 'before entering' it is a halt off it (rel.occupies), short of it along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along along st.lane_direction) and within the stop-point tolerance (st.region_geometry). (2) 'if there is no crosswalk' holds where the crosswalk lists are observed and none marks c; the st.stop_line recorded as marking c is then the place: a halt not past it, body within the tolerance; 'clearly marked' is read by the represented line (status). (3) 'if none': no stop line marks c either; the point nearest the intersecting highway before entering is c's entrance end at r (st.intersection): a halt off r, short of it along c's direction, body within the tolerance — the point nearest the intersecting highway and the one with the widest view along it. 'approaching traffic on the intersecting highway' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('using any highway for purposes of travel', carried as rel.occupies of a st.highway): the road users whose danger of a crash with the subject makes the stop 'required for safety' (operationalization of s3).

operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a stop is required for safety where, at some observation of the approach, some other road user of traffic (the traffic of s4, occupying a highway) and the subject approach each other within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), the envelope within which two bodies collide or nearly collide

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that enters an intersection r at the judged observation t — its footprint overlaps r at t and not at t-1 (rel.occupies) — having occupied at t-1 a carrier c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is r (st.lane_enters(c, r)) and which a yield sign (dev.yield_sign) governs (dev.governs); and a stop was required for safety: at some observation from the approach start (as defined in the obligation) to t-1, some road user u other than the subject (not same) that is traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway) satisfies prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) and prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) < p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where no observation of that stretch shows such a road user, the duty does not arise.
obligation: Duty of an act before an event (approach convention). Event: the entry into r at t through c; the duty is judged at t. Act: a halt of the subject (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance) at the governing place, read through c. Place, in the order the words list: (1) where a crosswalk x is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of(x, c)): a halt at which the footprint does not overlap x (rel.occupies), the subject is short of x along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along of x along st.lane_direction of c, positive) and the body-to-x ground distance (st.region_geometry) is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (2) else, where the crosswalk lists are observed and none marks c, and a stop line l is recorded as marking c: a halt at which the subject is not past l along c's direction and the body-to-l distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (3) else, where the crosswalk and stop-line lists are observed and none marks c: a halt at which the footprint does not overlap r, the subject is short of r along c's direction, and the body-to-r distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance. Where several marks of the governing kind mark c, a halt in the zone of any of them it has not passed counts. History bound: the search runs back from t-1 and ends at the approach start — the last observation before t at which the subject, on a carrier the governing mark is recorded as marking, is outside that mark's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it, farther than p.stop_point_tolerance; with several marks, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into r, whichever is later. Nothing else ends it: not the start of the recording, a first observation, another intersection or mark, or a distance travelled. Crossing the mark, moving on toward r, a change of carrier or lateral move within the same entry, a reverse within the zone and speed noise begin no new approach; only an observed exit from the zone upstream does. Verdict: the act found → compliant; the search reaches the approach start or the previous entry without it → violated; it reaches neither without the act → unknown. Missing evidence: the entry is unknown, never absent, where t-1 does not show the subject on a mapped carrier with an observed association to r; an unobserved dev.governs of c, an unobserved association of a mark with c, or an unobserved closest approach makes the verdict unknown only where it turns on it — a halt found at a place known to govern is compliant whatever the conflict reading, and a duty that does not arise is decided whatever the missing fact.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'approaching a yield sign' is read through a yield sign the source records as governing the approach carrier c that enters r; a sign recorded only as governing the intersection itself is not read as facing c.
'clearly marked' is read by the represented stop line; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

The point nearest the intersecting highway 'where the driver has a view of approaching traffic' is read as c's entrance end, the edge of r, within p.stop_point_tolerance: no point nearer the intersecting highway lies before the intersection, and the view along it is widest there; the view itself (st.sight_along_way) is not compared with a bound.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on lane c, governed by a yield sign, with a crosswalk marking c, approaches at 10 m/s while a car on the crossing highway is on a closest approach with it 2 s ahead at 1 m; the car never comes to rest and enters the intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same conflict; the car comes to rest 1 m short of the crosswalk, off it, lets the crossing car pass, and enters.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car approaches the yield sign alone in the scene, no road user is ever on a closest approach with it, and it enters without halting: no stop was required for safety.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions the yield sign governs.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No crosswalk marks c (lists observed); a stop line marks c; with the conflict present, the car comes to rest 1 m short of the line and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Neither a crosswalk nor a stop line marks c (lists observed); with the conflict present, the car comes to rest 1 m short of the intersection's edge, off it, and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A crosswalk marks c; the conflict is present on the approach; the car rests 20 m short of the crosswalk, moves on and enters without halting again.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already 1 m short of the crosswalk marking c, moving at 3 m/s, while a crossing car is on a closest approach with it 2 s ahead at 1 m; it enters without a recorded halt and no recorded observation shows it outside the stopping zone upstream.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the observation at which the car was outside the crosswalk's stopping zone upstream lies before the recording, so whether it halted within the zone before the recording began is not observed

segmentation.text: No vehicle
shall at any time be driven
through or within a safety zone.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; claimed as the aggregate. Same mapping as the index's 'No vehicle'.

'be driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven. Moving is the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance'). 'at any time' makes every observation a judged one.

'safety zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-057: 'the area officially set aside within a highway for the exclusive use of pedestrians and which is so plainly marked') is st.safety_zone, 'an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only'; 'through or within' it is the vehicle's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (..., safety zone, ...)').

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is moving at the observation: not drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance.
obligation: At every such observation the subject's footprint overlaps no safety zone: for every region z of kind st.safety_zone, not rel.occupies(subject, z).

narrowings.why: 'be driven' is read through the vehicle's motion: a moving vehicle is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
A safety zone 'officially set aside' and 'plainly marked' is read by the presence of the marked st.safety_zone region.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car moving at 8 m/s crosses a marked safety zone: its footprint overlaps the zone at several observations.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car moving at 8 m/s passes beside the safety zone, its footprint never overlapping it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car stays at rest at the curb for the whole recording.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car moves past a safety zone; the source does not report which regions the car's footprint overlaps.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle:
Shall not back into an intersection, on or over a crosswalk, or around a street corner.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

'back' is moving backward, drv.motion.moving_backward ('the component of a's velocity along a's heading ... below minus speed_tol'), read from kinematics as kin.gear's contract requires. 'into an intersection' is the footprint coming to overlap an intersection r (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies true at the observation, false at the previous one) while backing; the crosswalk and the stop line are not stand-ins for it, as st.intersection's contract says. 'on or over a crosswalk' is the backing vehicle's footprint overlapping a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'). 'around a street corner': the corner is where two streets meet; backing around it carries the vehicle through the area 'embraced within the prolongation ... of the lateral curb lines' of the meeting ways (DEF-NRS-484A-105), the st.intersection region, while its heading turns — read as backing with the footprint overlapping r, the heading having changed by at least the turn threshold since the backing within r began (Term.headingSince, integrated from kin.yaw_rate).

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is backing at the observation: drv.motion.moving_backward(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance.
obligation: At the observation, none of: (a) for some intersection r (st.intersection), the subject's footprint overlaps r and did not at the previous observation (rel.occupies) — it backs into r; (b) for some crosswalk x (st.crosswalk), the footprint overlaps x (rel.occupies); (c) for some intersection r, the footprint overlaps r and the magnitude of Term.headingSince(subject, p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, ψ) is at least p.turn_heading_min, where ψ = drv.motion.moving_backward(subject) and rel.occupies(subject, r): since it last began backing within r its heading has turned at least by the turn threshold — it backs around the corner.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'back into an intersection' is read as the entry into the intersection while backing; backing straight out of an intersection the vehicle is already in is not backing into it.

'around a street corner' is read through the intersection region the corner bounds, with a heading change of at least p.turn_heading_min while backing within it; the city-limit qualifier of 'street' (DEF-NRS-484A-265) is not read, every intersection's corners being treated as street corners.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car backs at 2 m/s along a street and its footprint comes to overlap the intersection while backing.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car backs at 2 m/s mid-block, away from any intersection or crosswalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives forward through an intersection and over its crosswalks without ever backing.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint comes to overlap an intersection while the source supplies no velocity, so whether it was backing is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car backs over a marked mid-block crosswalk: its footprint overlaps the crosswalk while backing.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car that overshot into the intersection backs straight out of it, heading unchanged, on an approach with no crosswalk: it is not entering the intersection and its heading has not turned.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A car standing within the intersection backs around the corner into the cross street, its heading turning 80 degrees while its footprint still overlaps the intersection.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; turning-movement classification in trajectory analysis

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle:
Shall in every case yield
the right-of-way
to moving traffic and pedestrians.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

The line is subsection (3) of 'Limitations on backing': 'in every case' is every case of backing, drv.motion.moving_backward ('the component of a's velocity along a's heading ... below minus speed_tol'). To yield is to grant precedence: the backing vehicle does not keep backing into a danger of a crash with the road users of s4, and does not touch them (rel.contact: 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)').

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'): the scene condition 'using any highway' is carried beside it as rel.occupies of a st.highway; 'moving' is the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt. 'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; since traffic already contains moving pedestrians, the words add pedestrians whether moving or not.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: circumstances of direction, speed and proximity giving rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: direction, speed and proximity give rise to the danger of a crash where, under constant velocities, the two road users approach each other within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance)

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is backing at the observation: drv.motion.moving_backward(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance.
obligation: At the observation, for every road user u other than the subject (not same) that is either moving traffic — ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway), and not drv.motion.complete_halt(u) with p.halt_speed_tolerance — or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): not rel.contact(subject, u), and not [prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) and prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) < p.conflict_centre_clearance].

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

The duty is read on a backing vehicle: the line is a subsection of the section limiting backing, and 'in every case' covers every case of backing; yielding is read as backing into no danger of a crash and no contact with the road users the words name.

scenarios.name: permit

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source supplies no velocity for the car, so whether it is backing is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car backs toward a parked car at rest 6 m behind it, closing at 1 m/s; the parked car is not moving traffic and not a pedestrian.

scenarios.name: branch_2
